Job Description

This Opportunity

Provides technical assistance and guidance for multi-site/phase environmental work processes, due diligence, subsurface investigation, and remediation projects. Conducts geophysical surveys and performs analysis of geological data from various media (soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, air/vapor). Substantiates reports and documentation to advise on field conditions, movement, and outcome of overall risks to ecological and human health. Assists project leadership with site assessment, corrective strategies, classification of contaminated materials, and assisting with their treatment, disposal, and/or onsite remediation. Ensures that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.

Your Impact

Determine well-defined data collection methods for extracting, identifying, and compiling environmental data from soil sampling, soil gas sampling, groundwater sampling, stormwater sampling, boring logs, and other matrices for projects, investigations, and surveys.
Assist with environmental site assessments (Phase I and II).
Research environmental hazmat databases regarding historical property land uses.
Coordinate site investigation, subsurface boring and trenching oversight, and monitoring of groundwater and extraction well installations.
Assist with oversight of drilling subcontractors during sample collection, well installations, and well abandonment.
Prepare data and visualizations such as mineral charts, soil analyses, groundwater modeling, maps geologic cross-sections, and other illustrations.
Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurements, analysis, and reporting.
Assist with development and scoping of medium-sized projects.
Generate complete, accurate, and concise documentation using electronic systems and field/work site notebook.
Prepare technical reports and presentations that explain research, findings, and recommendations to prevent, control, restore, or clean-up chemical and environmental problems and contamination.
Oversee equipment/tool performance, calibration, troubleshooting of malfunctions, and inventory control.
Assist in the analysis, evaluation, and interpretation of geologic, hydrogeologic, and chemical data obtained during field investigations, offering input with developing action plans for moderate- to high-level threat mitigation activities.
Work with cross-functional teams in executing project work.
Comply with safety guidelines and site-specific procedures which include but is not limited to, the maintenance of sample collection, trench and boring, laboratory documentation, written procedures, monitoring systems, and logbooks.
Prepare and implement site Health and Safety Plans (HASPs).
Comply with regulatory requirements pertaining to the data integrity, documentation, procedures, training, monitoring systems, and record compliance and retention.
Interact with regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and clients in a confident and professional manner.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, or closely related discipline.
5 to 7 years of experience working as a Geologist.
Analytical skills, and proficient with geological research techniques and protocol.
Working knowledge with the concepts of reducing and eliminating the use or generation of hazardous substances, processes, or products., and mitigation programs.
Working knowledge of relevant environmental laws, regulations, compliance practices, and record-keeping requirements.
Experience sampling soil and groundwater via drilling including direct-push, hollow-stem auger, and other similar drilling methods.
Experience in conducting Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM guidelines and industry standards.
Experience with UST investigations and remediation including investigation of hydro-carbon impacted sites.
Experience with evaluation of vapor intrusion and sampling soil gas per DTSC and EPA guidelines.
Experience installing groundwater monitoring wells, remediation wells, and soil gas wells.
Experience writing groundwater monitoring reports and well installation reports.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a scientific and non-scientific audience.
Highly capable self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Ability to work independently and provide guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Proficiency with technical writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.
Developed critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to reach conclusions from testing results, data collation, and identify the most cost-effective responses that will minimize waste, prevent pollution, and conserve resources.
Ability to assertively direct others in the field such as subcontracted drillers, excavation contractors, utility locators, and others to consistently complete tasks safely and efficiently.

Ingram Engineering Services, Inc. is a full-service geotechnical and structural engineering firm providing practical, real-world solutions since 2007. Our team takes a solutions-first approach, combining attention to detail, procedural discipline, and field expertise with laboratory testing and engineering insight. The result is accurate, reliable testing and oversight, plus practical recommendations and alternatives that help projects move forward on schedule with economical solutions in real time.

Position Overview
Ingram Engineering is seeking a motivated Geotechnical Laboratory Technician / Field Technician / Construction Materials Testing Technician
for immediate hire. This role offers the opportunity to work in a full-service AASHTO-accredited soils and materials testing laboratory at our West Chester, Pennsylvania location, as well as performing field work onsite on active construction projects throughout Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland in support of residential, commercial, land development, and infrastructure projects.
The ideal candidate enjoys hands-on work, can learn and repeat specific laboratory testing procedures that adhere to strict standards, and is comfortable solving problems in real time in field environments. This role provides exposure to a wide array of laboratory testing procedures as well as land development and construction processes, inspection procedures, engineering standards, and sample logging and collection methods in the field.
This Technician position plays a key role in supporting laboratory testing production and accuracy, project quality, documentation of field conditions, and communication of conditions, results, and findings to engineers, contractors, and project teams.

Responsibilities
Geotechnical Laboratory Testing Technician (Predominant Role) Perform standard geotechnical laboratory testing procedures on soil, aggregate, concrete and masonry, asphalt, fireproofing, and rock samples in accordance with strict procedural requirements, accurately and efficiently, and to company quality standards. This is the first priority of the role.
Most commonly conducted laboratory tests:
Classification of Soils (USCS, AASHTO, USDA)
Sieve Analysis
Hydrometer Analysis
Atterberg Limits (Liquid Limit and Plastic Limit)
Moisture Content
Proctors (Standard and Modified)
Permeability (Constant Head and Falling Head)
Organic Content
CBR (California Bearing Ratio)
Compressive Strength Testing

Field Technician (Secondary Role) Support field technician activities including inspections, testing, oversight, and sampling of structural fill, rebar, concrete and masonry, asphalt, drilling and test pit oversight with soil sampling and logging, infiltration testing, and bearing capacity testing, as a supplementary role and as needed based on workload.
Most commonly conducted field tasks:
Perform and document field inspections and testing services on active construction projects.
Conduct concrete and masonry testing and sampling in accordance with project specifications and ACI/ASTM standards as applicable.
Perform field compaction testing using nuclear density gauges.
Perform bearing capacity testing using Dynamic Cone Penetrometer (DCP), Geoprobe equipment, and other field methods.
Conduct asphalt density testing and general construction materials testing and oversight services.
Perform infiltration testing using a double-ring infiltrometer.
Provide oversight, logging, testing, and sampling of drilling via Standard Penetration Testing (SPT) and excavation of test pits.
Perform inspections, sampling, and testing of Sprayed Fire-Resistive Materials (SFRMs).
Verify construction activities for compliance with approved plans, specifications, and project requirements.
Review and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and related documents.
Prepare and submit daily field reports documenting testing activities, observations, and inspection findings using company templates.
Observe, document, and communicate deficiencies or nonconformities while providing direct oversight and recommendations that lead to prompt resolution and timely construction production.
Maintain accurate field notes and communication records.
Complete weekly timesheets and expense reports accurately and on schedule.
Coordinate with contractors, project managers, engineers, and clients regarding field activities.
Maintain and transport testing equipment required for daily assignments.
Manage multiple project assignments while maintaining quality and schedule expectations.
Assist with additional construction observation and special inspection services as necessary.

Qualifications
High school diploma required. Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree, or technical education and experience in soils, construction, engineering technology, geology, civil engineering, or a related field preferred.
0 to 3+ years of experience in laboratory testing, construction materials testing, field inspections, or related construction, engineering, or laboratory work preferred.
Experience reading laboratory and field testing standards, project specifications, and construction drawings preferred.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Adobe Acrobat, and general computer applications.
Ability to work independently in the laboratory and on field projects on a regular basis. Initial orientation and training will be provided as needed.
Ability to follow directions, retain information, and repeat the specific procedures required for proper laboratory testing.
Ability to work directly with the Laboratory Manager to ensure testing services are completed efficiently, accurately, and within project schedules.
Strong communication and organizational skills.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather and site conditions throughout all seasons.
Ability to safely lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Valid driver’s license and reliable personal transportation required. Reimbursement is provided for personal transportation used for work activities.
Willingness to travel daily to project sites throughout Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland.

Preferred Experience
Experience with:
Geotechnical laboratory testing for engineering purposes
Concrete and masonry field testing and sampling
Nuclear density gauge testing
Bearing capacity testing including DCP and Geoprobe methods
Asphalt density testing
Construction observation and field inspections
Reading construction plans and specifications
Construction materials testing (CMT)
ICC inspection certifications, ACI Concrete Field Testing Technician Grade I certification, and special inspection certifications

What We Offer
Competitive hourly compensation ranging from $22 to $25 per hour based on experience and certifications.
Competitive benefits package.
A varied and flexible work schedule with experience spanning a wide breadth of tasks.
Hands-on training and mentorship from experienced laboratory staff, engineers, and field staff.
Opportunity for career growth and advancement.
Exposure to diverse project types ranging from residential developments to commercial and infrastructure projects.
Collaborative, family-oriented company culture.
Overtime opportunities during peak construction seasons at time-and-a-half for hours worked over 40 per week.
Typical field schedules begin around 7:00 AM and generally conclude by approximately 3:00 PM, with daily schedules provided in advance.
Typical laboratory schedules begin around 8:00 or 9:00 AM and generally conclude by approximately 4:00 PM or 5:00 PM, depending on daily factors.

IES pairs a full-service, AASHTO-accredited laboratory with active geotechnical, structural, and special inspection work. That combination gives technicians unusually broad exposure: you see the sample collected in the field and you run the test that informs the recommendation. Our team works closely across disciplines, and laboratory staff report directly to our Laboratory Manager, who oversees our Quality Management System and accreditation program.
Hands-on work across both laboratory and field environments
Accredited laboratory with defined procedures and quality oversight
Diverse project types across PA, NJ, DE, and MD
Direct mentorship from experienced technicians, inspectors, and engineers
Clear path toward ACI, ICC, and NICET certifications
Collaborative, family-first culture

Classification of Soils (USCS, AASHTO, USDA)
Sieve Analysis
Hydrometer Analysis
Atterberg Limits (Liquid Limit and Plastic Limit)
Moisture Content
Proctors (Standard and Modified)
Permeability (Constant Head and Falling Head)
Organic Content
CBR (California Bearing Ratio)
Compressive Strength Testing

Asphalt density testing
Construction observation and field inspections
